# TCB Allowed List — Nanvix phys-mm

Any `external_body` outside this list must be removed.

## Allowed `external_body`

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::instance` — materializes a `&'static mut Inner` from the
  module-level `static mut INSTANCE: MaybeUninit<Inner>` singleton (guarded by `INSTANCE_INIT`).
  Raw-memory op over externally-owned `static mut` storage Verus cannot verify without a
  `PointsTo` (mirrors `bump_allocator`/`raw-array`). `ensures` pins the singleton's abstract
  state to `phys_view().frames`, asserts `(*r).inv()`, and records `phys_view().initialized` —
  the §8 ghost-token attachment for the singleton frame allocator.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref_mut`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::clear`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::new` — wraps a `FrameAddress` into an owning
  kernel-frame handle. Its body calls `crate::mm::virt::identity_map_page`, whose precondition is
  the **global** `identity_map_view().inv()`. That fact is owned by the `mm::virt` identity-map
  ghost token (a parameter-free singleton-global, like `phys_view()`), which is not realized in the
  `mm::phys` module and cannot be derived from the only available precondition (`base.inv()`). So
  the body cannot discharge the callee's `requires` in-scope. Same cross-module global-token
  deferral as `frame::book`/`frame::alloc` (post-mutation `phys_view()`): `external_body` until
  `mm::virt`'s identity-map token is realized, at which point `new` can pass it to
  `identity_map_page` and be verified in-body. `ensures Ok(kf) => kf@ == base@ && kf.inv()` (the
  address is preserved and page-aligned); `kframe`'s siblings `base`/`drop` verify in-body.
- `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc` — materializes a
  `&'static mut [u8; N]` from a backend-provided address (`usize as *mut`); raw-memory
  op Verus cannot verify without a `PointsTo` for the externally-owned `BssStorage`
  region. Mirrors `src/libs/raw-array`. `ensures` states alignment + in-bounds over
  the abstract `bump_view`.
- `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc_as` — delegates to
  `alloc` and re-materializes the slot as `&'static mut MaybeUninit<T>`; same rationale.
  `ensures` adds the `size_of::<T>()`/`align_of::<T>()` vs `(N, A)` guard arms.

## `external_body` introduced while speccing `arch::x86::mem::paging::table`

- `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs::Table::<E>::read` — reads a `TableEntry` from a
  page-table slot through a raw pointer materialized from `self.base` (`usize as *const E::Word`).
  Verus does not support `usize`→pointer casts (int-to-ptr materialization of externally-owned,
  volatile page-table memory), so the body cannot be verified. Same trust-boundary rationale as
  `bump_allocator::alloc` (`usize as *mut`) and `frame::instance`. See
  `nanvix-phys-arch-paging-table/verus-unsupported.md`. **The function is not contract-free:** it
  carries a full `#[verus_spec]` pinned to the global page-table-memory ghost — `requires index@ <
  PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`, `ensures result == spec_table_read::<E>(self@.addr, index@)` — exactly as
  `frame::instance` pins its result to `phys_view()` (parameter-free global ghost, no signature
  change).
- `src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs::Table::<E>::write` — writes a `TableEntry` into a
  page-table slot through a raw pointer materialized from `self.base` (`usize as *mut E::Word`).
  Same int-to-ptr / volatile externally-owned-memory limitation as `read`. Carries only the sound
  `requires index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` (auto from `TableIndex::inv`); it has **no** contents
  `ensures`. A contents postcondition pinning the *pure* global ghost `spec_table_word(self@.addr,
  index@)` to the caller-chosen `entry` would be unsound for an `external_body` (assumed)
  contract: two writes of distinct entries to the same slot would assume
  `spec_entry_raw(e1) == spec_entry_raw(e2)`, which with `lemma_entry_roundtrip` derives
  `e1 == e2`, i.e. `false` (Turn 2 review #2/#3/#15; exploit reproduced). The genuine `old@ -> @`
  slot-update transition (`self@.entries[index@] == Some(entry)`, other slots framed) is therefore
  **deferred to the proving-phase page-table permission token**, exactly the `identity_map_view()`
  `v -> v'` deferral convention in `identity_map.spec.rs`.

19.     pub initialized: bool,

22.     /// address. Membership means: the page is **present, writable, supervisor-only**, and
23.     /// reachable at its own physical address in the kernel address space. Permissions are uniform

56. impl IdentityMapView {
57.     /// Implementation-consistency invariant (e.g. the abstract `mapped` set agrees with the

4. //!
5. //! # Description
6. //!
7. //! This module implements identity mapping for physical memory accesses.
8. //!
9. //! Only the kernel process has physical memory identity-mapped into its virtual address space.
10. //! At boot, page tables are allocated from BSS for kernel code/data/bss/modules. During
11. //! [`init`], page tables for every PDE index in `[0, MEMORY_SIZE)` are pre-allocated from the
12. //! BSS pool, covering all physical memory. If a frame is later allocated outside these
13. //! pre-covered ranges, [`identity_map_page`] lazily installs a page table entry (and, when
14. //! necessary, a new page table from the BSS pool) for the corresponding PDE.
15. //!
16. //! When a new user address space is created, [`sync_kernel_pdes`] copies all present kernel
17. //! identity-mapping PDEs into the new page directory in a single pass.
18. 
19. //==================================================================================================
20. // Imports
21. //==================================================================================================

24. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
25. include!("identity_map.spec.rs");

104. /// # Parameters

106. /// - `kernel_pd_paddr`: Physical address of the kernel page directory.

1. # View Design: `mm::virt::identity_map`
2. 
3. ## Abstract Resource
4. 
5. To callers, this module is the **kernel's identity map**: a single global,
6. write-and-supervisor mapping that answers one question — *"is this physical page
7. reachable at its own physical address (V == P) in the kernel address space?"* —
8. and, when asked, makes it so without consuming frame-allocator memory.
9. 
10. It is a process-wide **singleton** (backed by the `KERNEL_PD_PADDR` / `KERNEL_CR3`
11. statics plus a BSS page-table pool). The in-scope functions are free functions,
12. not methods on an exec struct, so the View models the *global* identity-map state
13. rather than the contents of any one passed-in `Table`. How that global ghost
14. state is threaded (ghost global vs. tracked token) is a specification-phase
15. concern; this document fixes only the abstraction.
16. 
17. ## View Struct
18. 
19. ```rust
20. /// Abstract state of the kernel identity map.
21. ///
22. /// This is a ghost model of global state — there is no owning exec struct.
23. pub struct IdentityMapView {
24.     /// Whether the lazy identity mapper has been initialized (i.e. `init` has
25.     /// published the kernel page directory). Before initialization the boot
26.     /// page tables are still active and every `identity_map_page` is a
27.     /// successful no-op, so this flag selects which transition applies.
28.     pub initialized: bool,
29. 
30.     /// The set of identity-mapped pages, each identified by its page-aligned
31.     /// physical base address. Membership means: the page is **present,
32.     /// writable, supervisor-only**, and reachable at its own physical address
33.     /// in the kernel address space. Permissions are uniform across all mapped
34.     /// pages, so they are encoded by membership rather than stored per page.
35.     ///
36.     /// Implementation note: realized as `Set<int>` (not `Set<usize>`) in
37.     /// `identity_map.spec.rs`, because `PhysicalAddress@` and
38.     /// `PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>@` both view as `int`. This keeps
39.     /// `mapped.contains(phys_addr@)` and `spec_page_base(..)` typechecking
40.     /// directly and matches `FrameAllocView`'s address element type.
41.     pub mapped: Set<int>,,
42. }
43. ```
44. 
45. ### Spec functions (signatures designed here; bodies are spec-phase work)
46. 
47. ```rust
48. impl /* global identity map */ {
49.     /// Maps concrete (global) state to the abstract identity map.
50.     /// Public so callers can name the abstract state; closed so the mapping
51.     /// from `KERNEL_PD_PADDR`, the page directory, and the page-table pool
52.     /// does not leak.
53.     pub closed spec fn view(/* ghost global */) -> IdentityMapView;
54. }
55. 
56. impl IdentityMapView {
57.     /// Implementation-consistency invariant (e.g. the abstract `mapped` set
58.     /// agrees with the present PDE/PTE bits, page-table pool bounds, etc.).
59.     /// Cannot be written until implementation bodies are visible — left as a
60.     /// placeholder; the specification phase fills it in.
61.     pub closed spec fn internal_inv(self) -> bool {
62.         true
63.     }
64. }
65. ```
66. 
67. ## Well-formedness Invariant
68. 
69. ```rust
70. impl IdentityMapView {
71.     pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {
72.         &&& self.internal_inv()
73.         // Every recorded page is identified by a page-aligned base address.
74.         &&& (forall|p: usize| self.mapped.contains(p) ==> is_page_aligned(p))
75.         // Before initialization no lazy mapping has been installed; coverage
76.         // is provided entirely by the boot page tables.
77.         &&& (!self.initialized ==> self.mapped =~= Set::empty())
78.     }
79. }
80. ```
81. 
82. `is_page_aligned(p) := p % PAGE_SIZE == 0` is a free spec helper (constant
83. resolved in the spec phase). Both conjuncts are abstraction-level truths any
84. implementation maintains, not statements about a particular layout.
85. 
86. Monotonicity ("a mapped page is never unmapped or remapped") is a property of
87. *transitions*, so it lives in `ensures` (e.g. `old@.mapped.subset_of(self@.mapped)`),
88. not in `inv()`.
89. 
90. ## Spec Transition / Query Functions
91. 
92. ```rust
93. impl IdentityMapView {
94.     /// Page is reachable at its own physical address right now.
95.     /// Before init, the boot tables make every page reachable; after init,
96.     /// reachability is exactly membership in `mapped`. This is the headline
97.     /// resource callers obtain from `identity_map_page` on `Ok`.
98.     pub open spec fn accessible(self, page: usize) -> bool {
99.         !self.initialized || self.mapped.contains(page)
100.     }
101. 
102.     /// Unconditional install of one page (idempotent). Models the leaf step
103.     /// `ensure_pte` realizes: it always adds the page to the map.
104.     pub open spec fn spec_install_page(self, page: usize) -> IdentityMapView {
105.         IdentityMapView { mapped: self.mapped.insert(page), ..self }
106.     }
107. 
108.     /// Full effect of `identity_map_page`: install the page when the mapper is
109.     /// initialized, otherwise a no-op (boot tables already cover it). Either
110.     /// way the page ends up `accessible`.
111.     pub open spec fn spec_map_page(self, page: usize) -> IdentityMapView {
112.         if self.initialized {
113.             self.spec_install_page(page)
114.         } else {
115.             self
116.         }
117.     }
118. }
119. ```
120. 
121. ### How each in-scope function uses the View
122. 
123. | Function | View-level effect | Notes |
124. |----------|-------------------|-------|
125. | `identity_map_page(phys_addr)` | `self@ == old@.spec_map_page(base(phys_addr@))`; on `Ok`, `self@.accessible(base(phys_addr@))` | `base(a) := align_down(a, PAGE_SIZE)`; equals `a` for the page-aligned input. On `Err`, `self@ == old@` and the page need not be accessible. |
126. | `ensure_pte(pt, pte_idx, phys_addr)` | `self@ == old@.spec_install_page(base(phys_addr))` (idempotent) | The leaf step that realizes V==P; `identity_map_page` wraps it with the `initialized` guard. |
127. | `ensure_pt(pd, pde_idx)` | `self@.mapped == old@.mapped` (identity at the page abstraction) | Allocating/installing a page table establishes *internal structure* only — its PTEs start absent, so no page becomes mapped. Returns an opaque page-aligned `pt_paddr`. Idempotent: a present PDE leaves state unchanged. Also called by `init` to pre-allocate. |
128. 
129. The two private helpers deliberately have **no PDE/PTE-index fields in the
130. View**: the caller analysis states callers "don't care about the page-directory /
131. page-table index split." `ensure_pt` contributes nothing to `mapped`; only
132. `ensure_pte` does. Their composition inside `identity_map_page` is exactly
133. `spec_map_page`.
134. 
135. ## Design Rationale
136. 
137. **`initialized: bool`** — The contract has a genuine pre-init mode: before `init`
138. publishes the kernel PD, `identity_map_page` succeeds as a no-op and the page is
139. reachable through boot tables. This flag is the minimal abstract state needed to
140. state that conditional transition (`spec_map_page`) and to make `accessible`
141. total. *Substitution test:* any lazy-mapper implementation has a "not yet set up,
142. boot tables cover memory" phase versus an "active" phase; the flag survives a
143. rewrite. It is never a stand-in for the concrete `KERNEL_PD_PADDR == 0` check —
144. callers observe a *mode*, not an atomic.
145. 
146. **`mapped: Set<usize>`** — The core resource: which physical pages are
147. identity-mapped (present + writable + supervisor). Callers reason purely in terms
148. of set membership ("is my frame reachable?"), and idempotence/monotonicity are
149. naturally `insert` / `subset_of` on a `Set`. *Substitution test:* every possible
150. implementation — two-level x86 tables, a flat array, a different paging scheme —
151. must track *which pages are mapped*; the set is implementation-agnostic. Elements
152. are page-aligned base addresses (`usize`) because callers already hold
153. `PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>` and the skill keeps addresses as `usize`; this
154. avoids introducing division/frame-number arithmetic at the abstraction surface.
155. 
156. **Permissions encoded by membership, not a field** — These functions only ever
157. create writable, supervisor mappings, so per-page permission state would be a
158. constant. Folding "writable + supervisor" into the meaning of `mapped`
159. membership keeps the View minimal while still letting `KernelFrame::clear` /
160. `memset` rely on writability.
161. 
162. **`accessible` as a derived query** — Gives callers a single predicate for the
163. postcondition they actually want ("the frame is reachable now") that is uniform
164. across the pre-init and post-init cases, so caller proofs don't branch on
165. `initialized`.
166. 
167. **`inv()` conjuncts** — `is_page_aligned` over `mapped` is the abstraction's
168. well-formedness (a "page" is a page-aligned unit). The `!initialized ==> mapped
169. empty` conjunct is the cross-field consistency that justifies `spec_map_page`'s
170. no-op branch (nothing is silently dropped when not initialized). Both are
171. caller-visible truths and hold for any implementation.
172. 
173. **Field usage (minimality check)** — `initialized` is used in `spec_map_page`,
174. `accessible`, and `inv`; `mapped` is used in every spec function. No field is
175. dead.
176. 
177. | Criterion | Result |
178. |-----------|--------|
179. | Substitution | ✅ both fields survive a full rewrite |
180. | Caller-only | ✅ no PDE/PTE indices, flag bits, BSS-pool, or CR3 mechanics leak |
181. | Complete | ✅ accessibility, idempotence, monotonicity, pre-init no-op all expressible |
182. | Minimal | ✅ two fields, both referenced by specs |
183. | No code-as-spec | ✅ describes *which pages are mapped*, not *how* |
184. 
185. ## Rejected Alternatives
186. 
187. - **Two-level `Map<TableIndex, Map<TableIndex, usize>>` (PD → PT → frame).**
188.   Mirrors the x86 page-table structure and the `ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte` split.
189.   Rejected: the caller analysis explicitly says external callers don't care about
190.   the PD/PT index split or `Table::from_address` mechanics — this is an
191.   abstraction leak (Over-Faithful anti-pattern). The page-granular `Set` captures
192.   everything callers observe.
193. 
194. - **`mapped: Set<nat>` keyed by frame number (`addr / PAGE_SIZE`).** Equivalent
195.   power, but forces division semantics into the abstraction and diverges from the
196.   `PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>` (a `usize`) callers actually pass. Page-aligned
197.   `usize` base addresses are more directly usable in caller specs.
198. 
199. - **Per-page permission/flags field (e.g. `Map<usize, Perms>`).** All mappings
200.   are uniformly writable + supervisor, so this would store a constant. Encoded by
201.   `mapped` membership instead.
202. 
203. - **A `pt_pool_used: nat` / remaining-BSS-slots field.** Callers explicitly don't
204.   care about page-table-pool bookkeeping; `OutOfMemory` is observed only as an
205.   `Err`. Exhaustion is a failure outcome, not abstract state callers reason about.
206.   Belongs (if anywhere) inside `internal_inv()`, not the public View.
207. 
208. - **`kernel_pd_paddr: usize` / `cr3` fields.** These are concrete handles to the
209.   paging structures, not caller-observable abstract state. Callers never name the
210.   kernel PD address; replacing it (or the CR3 root) with a different mechanism
211.   must not change the spec. Leaking them fails the substitution test.
212. 
213. - **A separate per-`Table` View for `ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte`.** Tempting because
214.   they take a `Table` argument, but they are private sub-steps of a single global
215.   operation; giving them independent View types would fragment the abstraction and
216.   re-expose the index structure. They are specified as refinements of
217.   `spec_install_page` / the identity transition on the one global
218.   `IdentityMapView`.
219. 
220. - **No `initialized` flag (treat init as just another mapping).** Then
221.   `identity_map_page`'s pre-init no-op success could not be stated precisely, and
222.   `accessible` would wrongly require `mapped` membership during early boot. The
223.   flag is the minimal addition that captures the documented pre-init transparency.
224.

# Troubleshooting Nanvix

Use this skill when the user reports problems, errors, or unexpected behavior while developing,
building, or running Nanvix. This covers common failure modes and their resolutions.

## Resource Leaks and Cleanup

Crashes or abnormal termination may leave stale resources.  Clean them up with:

### Quick Cleanup

```bash
# Remove all stale Nanvix resources.
sudo rm -rf /tmp/nvx:*
rm -rf /tmp/nanvix-test-*
sudo rm -rf /tmp/clh-console
sudo rm -f /tmp/cloud-hypervisor.sock
sudo rm -f /tmp/*.socket

# Clean up stale network namespaces (L2 deployments).
for ns in $(sudo ip netns list 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -o 'nvxns-[0-9]*' || true); do
  sudo ip link del "nvxgw-h-${ns#nvxns-}" \
      2>/dev/null || true
  sudo ip netns del "${ns}" 2>/dev/null || true
done
```

There is also a cleanup script for `nanvixd` resources:

```bash
./scripts/cleanup-nanvixd.sh
```

### Resource Types

| Resource           | Location            | Created By     |
|--------------------|---------------------|----------------|
| Temp directories   | `/tmp/nvx:*`        | `nanvixd`      |
| Test directories   | `/tmp/nanvix-test-*`| Unit tests     |
| Unix sockets       | `/tmp/*.socket`     | `syscomm`      |
| Network namespaces | `nvxns-*`           | L2 deployments |
| Cloud Hypervisor   | `/tmp/clh-console`  | L2 snapshot    |

## Build Failures

### Toolchain Not Found

**Symptom**: Cargo toolchain errors or missing tools.

**Fix**: Ensure the `toolchain/` symlink points to a valid installation:

```bash
ls -la toolchain/
# If missing, rebuild:
./z setup --nanvix-sdk --toolchain-dir $HOME/toolchain
ln -s $HOME/toolchain toolchain
```

### Full Reset (Last Resort)

**Symptom**: Build or test issues persist after normal cleanup.

**Fix**: Perform a full cleanup, then rebuild:

```bash
./z distclean

./z build -- all
```

### sccache Crashes

**Symptom**: Intermittent build failures with sccache errors.

**Fix**: sccache is automatically disabled for non-artifact targets. For manual builds, unset it:

```bash
./z build -- all SCCACHE=
```

## Runtime Failures

### KVM Not Available

**Symptom**: `Could not access KVM kernel module` or
similar.

**Fix**:

```bash
sudo kvm-ok
sudo lsmod | grep kvm
sudo usermod -aG kvm $USER
newgrp kvm
```

### Port Already in Use

**Symptom**: `Address already in use` when starting `nanvixd` in HTTP mode.

**Fix**: Kill existing processes or use a different port:

```bash
lsof -i :8080
kill <PID>
# Or use different port:
./bin/nanvixd.elf -http-addr 127.0.0.1:9090
```

### TIME_WAIT Socket Connections

**Symptom**: After L2 deployments, connections linger.

**Fix**: Check and wait for them to clear:

```bash
ss -tan | grep 8181
```

### Tests Fail Due to Stale Resources

**Symptom**: CI tests fail with resource-exists or port-in-use errors.

**Fix**: Run the full cleanup script (see Resource Leaks section above).

## Debugging

### Enable Verbose Logging

```bash
# Nanvixd daemon logging.
RUST_LOG=debug ./bin/nanvixd.elf \
    -console-file /dev/stdout \
    -- ./bin/hello-rust-nostd.elf
RUST_LOG=trace ./bin/nanvixd.elf \
    -http-addr 127.0.0.1:8080

# Build with trace-level guest logging.
./z build -- all LOG_LEVEL=trace
```

### Standalone UserVM Debugging

Bypass the full stack for low-level kernel debugging:

```bash
RUST_LOG=debug ./bin/uservm.elf \
    -kernel ./bin/kernel.elf \
    -initrd ./bin/hello-rust-nostd.elf \
    -standalone
```

### Check Build Errors

```bash
# Rust check with JSON output for IDE integration.
./z build -- check
```

### Log Files

Runtime logs are stored under `logs/` with timestamped
directory names (e.g., `logs/2026_02_24_13_04_54/`).

## Windows-Specific Issues

### WHP Not Enabled

**Symptom**: UserVM fails to start with hypervisor-related errors.

**Fix**:

```powershell
# Run in an elevated PowerShell prompt.
Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName HypervisorPlatform -All
# Restart the machine.
```

### Symlink Errors on Windows Clone

**Symptom**: Build or tool errors because Git checked out symlinks as text files.

**Fix**: Re-clone with Developer Mode enabled and symlinks flag:

```powershell
git clone -c core.symlinks=true https://github.com/nanvix/nanvix.git
```

To repair an existing clone (including an optional backup of local changes):

```powershell
# Optional: back up any local changes before resetting the working tree.
git status
# Either commit your work-in-progress, or stash it:
# git commit -am "WIP backup"
# git stash -u

git config core.symlinks true
git checkout -- .
```

490. /// allocates a new page table from the BSS pool, installs the PDE, and returns the new page
491. /// table's physical address.
492. ///
493. /// # Parameters
494. ///
495. /// - `pd`: The kernel page directory table.
496. /// - `pde_idx`: The page directory index to check.
497. ///
498. /// # Returns
499. ///
500. /// Upon success, the physical address of the page table is returned. Upon failure, an error is
501. /// returned instead.
502. ///
503. /// # Errors
504. ///
505. /// - [`ErrorCode::InvalidArgument`]: Failed to read the PDE.
506. /// - [`ErrorCode::OutOfMemory`]: No BSS page table slots available.
507. /// - [`ErrorCode::BadAddress`]: The allocated page table frame number is out of range.
508. ///
509. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
510. #[verus_spec(result =>
511.     requires
512.         identity_map_view().inv(),
513.     ensures
514.         match result {
515.             // The returned page-table physical address is page-aligned (BSS-backed and
516.             // immediately usable as `Table::from_address` for the follow-up `ensure_pte`).
517.             // Ensuring a page table installs internal structure only -- it adds no page to the
518.             // identity map. The global map remains well-formed.
519.             Ok(pt_paddr) => {
520.                 &&& identity_map_view().inv()
521.                 &&& spec_is_page_aligned(pt_paddr as int)
522.             },
523.             // On failure no usable page-table address is produced and the identity map is left
524.             // well-formed: `ensure_pt` only ever installs *empty* page tables, so it maps no
525.             // page on either path (`mapped` is unaffected). A stronger `mapped`-equality
526.             // postcondition would require threading the pre-state (`old@`), but `ensure_pt`'s
527.             // signature is fixed -- its other caller `init` is out of scope and must not be
528.             // touched -- so invariant preservation is the strongest sound failure-state fact
529.             // expressible over the parameterless global view here. This is *not* `true`: it
530.             // guarantees a failed `ensure_pt` never corrupts the abstract identity map.
531.             Err(_) => identity_map_view().inv(),
532.         },
533. )]
534. fn ensure_pt(pd: Table<PageDirectoryEntry>, pde_idx: TableIndex) -> Result<usize, Error> {
535.     let pde: PageDirectoryEntry = unsafe { pd.read(pde_idx) }.ok_or_else(|| {
536.         let reason: &str = "invalid PDE read from kernel PD";
537.         error!("ensure_pt(): {reason}");
538.         Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason)
539.     })?;
540. 
541.     if pde.is_present() {
542.         return Ok(pde.frame_address());
543.     }
544. 
545.     // No PT exists — allocate one from the BSS pool (zeroed = all PTEs absent).
546.     // SAFETY: atomic bump allocator ensures exclusive access to the slot;
547.     // BSS is zero-initialized, so assume_init_mut() is sound for integer arrays.
548.     let slot: &'static mut [PteWord; PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH] = unsafe {
549.         PAGE_TABLE_ALLOCATOR
550.             .alloc_as::<[PteWord; PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH]>()
551.             .map_err(|e| {
552.                 error!("ensure_pt(): page table allocation failed: {}", e);
553.                 Error::new(ErrorCode::OutOfMemory, "BSS page table allocation failed")
554.             })?
555.             .assume_init_mut()
556.     };
557.     let pt_paddr: usize = slot.as_ptr() as usize;
558. 
559.     // Install the PDE with type-safe flag constructors.
560.     let pt_frame: FrameNumber =
561.         FrameNumber::from_raw_value(pt_paddr / mem::PAGE_SIZE).ok_or_else(|| {
562.             let reason: &str = "BSS page table frame number out of range";
563.             error!("ensure_pt(): {reason}");
564.             Error::new(ErrorCode::BadAddress, reason)
565.         })?;
566.     let new_pde: PageDirectoryEntry = PageDirectoryEntry::new(
567.         PageDirectoryEntryFlags::new(
568.             PresentFlag::Present,
569.             ReadWriteFlag::ReadWrite,
570.             UserSupervisorFlag::Supervisor,
571.             PageWriteThroughFlag::NotWriteThrough,
572.             PageCacheDisableFlag::CacheEnabled,
573.             AccessedFlag::NotAccessed,
574.             DirtyFlag::NotDirty,
575.             PageSizeFlag::Standard,
576.         ),
577.         pt_frame,
578.     );

580.     unsafe { pd.write(pde_idx, new_pde) };

586. /// # Description
587. ///
588. /// Ensures that a page table entry for the given index is identity-mapped. If the PTE is already
589. /// present, this function is a no-op. Otherwise, it creates a new identity-mapped PTE and
590. /// invalidates the corresponding TLB entry.
591. ///
592. /// # Parameters
593. ///
594. /// - `pt`: The page table to write into.
595. /// - `pte_idx`: The page table index to check.

610.         identity_map_view().inv(),
611.     ensures
612.         identity_map_view().inv(),
613.         match result {
614.             // The leaf step that realizes V==P: on success the page containing `phys_addr` is
615.             // present (writable, supervisor) and reachable at its own physical address. Membership
616.             // holds whether the PTE was freshly installed or already present (idempotent).

618.             // On failure the leaf entry was not installed: the PTE was not already present (a

620.             // failure left it absent, so the page is *not* in the identity map. `identity_map_page`
621.             // propagates this and its caller must not treat the page as reachable.
622.             Err(_) => !identity_map_view().mapped.contains(spec_page_base(phys_addr as int)),
623.         },
624. )]

627.     pte_idx: TableIndex,
628.     phys_addr: usize,
629. ) -> Result<(), Error> {

632.         error!("ensure_pte(): {reason}");

638.     }
639.

641.     let frame: FrameNumber =
642.         FrameNumber::from_raw_value(phys_addr / mem::PAGE_SIZE).ok_or_else(|| {

644.             error!("ensure_pte(): {reason}");
645.             Error::new(ErrorCode::BadAddress, reason)
646.         })?;
647.     let new_pte: PageTableEntry = PageTableEntry::new(

650.             ReadWriteFlag::ReadWrite,
651.             UserSupervisorFlag::Supervisor,
652.             PageWriteThroughFlag::NotWriteThrough,
653.             PageCacheDisableFlag::CacheEnabled,
654.             AccessedFlag::NotAccessed,
655.             DirtyFlag::NotDirty,
656.         ),

671. /// Identity-maps a single page in the kernel page directory.
672. ///
673. /// If the target PTE is already present, this function is a no-op. If the PDE is absent, a new
674. /// page table is allocated from the BSS pool and installed before the identity-mapped PTE is
675. /// created.
676. ///
677. /// # Parameters
678. ///
679. /// - `phys_addr`: Page-aligned physical address to identity-map.
680. ///
681. /// # Returns
682. ///
683. /// Upon success, empty is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
684. ///
685. /// # Errors
686. ///
687. /// - [`ErrorCode::InvalidArgument`]: Failed to read a valid paging entry.
688. ///
689. /// # Notes
690. ///
691. /// If the lazy mapper has not been initialized yet (boot page tables still active), this function
692. /// is a no-op and returns success.
693. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
694. #[verus_spec(result =>
695.     requires
696.         identity_map_view().inv(),
697.     ensures
698.         identity_map_view().inv(),
699.         match result {
700.             // The page containing `phys_addr` is reachable at its own physical address. After init
701.             // this means it is present (writable, supervisor) in the kernel page directory; before
702.             // init the call is a no-op and the boot page tables already cover it. Either way the
703.             // caller (`KernelFrame::new`) may subsequently read/write the frame through `phys_addr`.
704.             Ok(_) => identity_map_view().accessible(phys_addr@),
705.             // On failure the page was *not* made accessible, so `KernelFrame::new` must propagate
706.             // the error and must not dereference the frame. This is sound: an `Err` is only
707.             // reachable post-init (the pre-init path returns `Ok` as a no-op), and on the failure
708.             // path the page was not already mapped (an already-present PTE returns `Ok`) and the
709.             // failed `ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte` did not map it -- so `accessible` is false. Mirrors
710.             // the `mm::phys` convention of stating the failure-state fact over the global view.
711.             Err(_) => !identity_map_view().accessible(phys_addr@),
712.         },
713. )]
714. pub(crate) fn identity_map_page(phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>) -> Result<(), Error> {
715.     let phys_addr: usize = phys_addr.into_raw_value();
716. 
717.     let pd_paddr: usize = KERNEL_PD_PADDR.load(Ordering::Acquire);
718.     // Check if the lazy mapper has been initialized.
719.     if pd_paddr == 0 {
720.         return Ok(());
721.     }
722. 
723.     let pde_idx: TableIndex = paging::pd_index(phys_addr);
724.     let pte_idx: TableIndex = paging::pt_index(phys_addr);
725. 
726.     // SAFETY: the PD is identity-mapped.
727.     let pd: Table<PageDirectoryEntry> = unsafe { Table::from_address(pd_paddr) };
728.     let pt_paddr: usize = ensure_pt(pd, pde_idx)?;
729. 
730.     // SAFETY: the PT is identity-mapped (BSS-backed).
731.     let pt: Table<PageTableEntry> = unsafe { Table::from_address(pt_paddr) };
732.     ensure_pte(pt, pte_idx, phys_addr)
733. }
734. 
735. //==================================================================================================
736. // Tests
737. //==================================================================================================
738. 
739. #[cfg(feature = "test")]
740. pub(super) mod test {
741.     use super::{
742.         sync_kernel_pdes,
743.         KERNEL_PD_PADDR,
744.     };
745.     use crate::{
746.         hal::mem::PageDirectoryAddress,
747.         mm::VirtMemoryManager,
748.     };
749.     use ::arch::mem::{
750.         self,
751.         paging::{
752.             self,
753.             PageDirectoryEntry,
754.             Table,
755.             TableIndex,
756.         },
757.     };
758.     use ::config::kernel::MEMORY_SIZE;
759.     use ::core::sync::atomic::Ordering;
760.

6. // Abstract state of the kernel identity map
7. //==================================================================================================

9. /// Abstract state of the kernel identity map (see `view_design.md`).

12. /// the `KERNEL_PD_PADDR` / `KERNEL_CR3` atomics plus a BSS page-table pool, so there is no owning
13. /// exec struct. Addresses use `int` (the `View` of `PhysicalAddress` / `PageAligned`), consistent

16.     /// Whether the lazy identity mapper has been initialized (i.e. `init` has published the kernel
17.     /// page directory). Before initialization the boot page tables are still active and every
18.     /// `identity_map_page` is a successful no-op, so this flag selects which transition applies.
19.     pub initialized: bool,
20. 
21.     /// The set of identity-mapped pages, each identified by its page-aligned physical base
22.     /// address. Membership means: the page is **present, writable, supervisor-only**, and
23.     /// reachable at its own physical address in the kernel address space. Permissions are uniform
24.     /// across all mapped pages, so they are encoded by membership rather than stored per page.
25.     pub mapped: Set<int>,
26. }

44.     addr % spec_page_size() == 0
45. }
46. 
47. /// The page-aligned base address of the page containing `addr`.
48. pub open spec fn spec_page_base(addr: int) -> int {
49.     addr - (addr % spec_page_size())
50. }
51. 
52. //==================================================================================================
53. // Invariants and queries
54. //==================================================================================================

56. impl IdentityMapView {
57.     /// Implementation-consistency invariant (e.g. the abstract `mapped` set agrees with the

59.     /// the proving phase fills it in once the concrete `view()` body is realized.

61.         true

68.         &&& (forall|p: int| #[trigger] self.mapped.contains(p) ==> spec_is_page_aligned(p))
69.         // Before initialization no lazy mapping has been installed; coverage is provided entirely
70.         // by the boot page tables.
71.         &&& (!self.initialized ==> self.mapped =~= Set::empty())
72.     }

74.     /// The page based at `page` is reachable at its own physical address right now. Before init the
75.     /// boot tables make every page reachable; after init reachability is exactly membership in
76.     /// `mapped`. This is the headline resource callers obtain from `identity_map_page` on `Ok`.
77.     pub open spec fn accessible(self, page: int) -> bool {
78.         !self.initialized || self.mapped.contains(page)
79.     }

81.     /// Unconditional install of one page (idempotent). Models the leaf step `ensure_pte` realizes:
82.     /// it always adds the page to the map.
83.     pub open spec fn spec_install_page(self, page: int) -> IdentityMapView {

88.     /// otherwise a no-op (boot tables already cover it). Either way the page ends up `accessible`.
89.     pub open spec fn spec_map_page(self, page: int) -> IdentityMapView {
90.         if self.initialized {
91.             self.spec_install_page(page)
92.         } else {
93.             self
94.         }
95.     }
96. }

1. # View Design: `mm::virt::identity_map`
2. 
3. ## Abstract Resource
4. 
5. To callers, this module is the **kernel's identity map**: a single global,
6. write-and-supervisor mapping that answers one question — *"is this physical page
7. reachable at its own physical address (V == P) in the kernel address space?"* —
8. and, when asked, makes it so without consuming frame-allocator memory.
9. 
10. It is a process-wide **singleton** (backed by the `KERNEL_PD_PADDR` / `KERNEL_CR3`
11. statics plus a BSS page-table pool). The in-scope functions are free functions,
12. not methods on an exec struct, so the View models the *global* identity-map state
13. rather than the contents of any one passed-in `Table`. How that global ghost
14. state is threaded (ghost global vs. tracked token) is a specification-phase
15. concern; this document fixes only the abstraction.
16. 
17. ## View Struct
18. 
19. ```rust
20. /// Abstract state of the kernel identity map.
21. ///
22. /// This is a ghost model of global state — there is no owning exec struct.
23. pub struct IdentityMapView {
24.     /// Whether the lazy identity mapper has been initialized (i.e. `init` has
25.     /// published the kernel page directory). Before initialization the boot
26.     /// page tables are still active and every `identity_map_page` is a
27.     /// successful no-op, so this flag selects which transition applies.
28.     pub initialized: bool,
29. 
30.     /// The set of identity-mapped pages, each identified by its page-aligned
31.     /// physical base address. Membership means: the page is **present,
32.     /// writable, supervisor-only**, and reachable at its own physical address
33.     /// in the kernel address space. Permissions are uniform across all mapped
34.     /// pages, so they are encoded by membership rather than stored per page.
35.     ///
36.     /// Implementation note: realized as `Set<int>` (not `Set<usize>`) in
37.     /// `identity_map.spec.rs`, because `PhysicalAddress@` and
38.     /// `PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>@` both view as `int`. This keeps
39.     /// `mapped.contains(phys_addr@)` and `spec_page_base(..)` typechecking
40.     /// directly and matches `FrameAllocView`'s address element type.
41.     pub mapped: Set<int>,,
42. }
43. ```
44. 
45. ### Spec functions (signatures designed here; bodies are spec-phase work)
46. 
47. ```rust
48. impl /* global identity map */ {
49.     /// Maps concrete (global) state to the abstract identity map.
50.     /// Public so callers can name the abstract state; closed so the mapping
51.     /// from `KERNEL_PD_PADDR`, the page directory, and the page-table pool
52.     /// does not leak.
53.     pub closed spec fn view(/* ghost global */) -> IdentityMapView;
54. }
55. 
56. impl IdentityMapView {
57.     /// Implementation-consistency invariant (e.g. the abstract `mapped` set
58.     /// agrees with the present PDE/PTE bits, page-table pool bounds, etc.).
59.     /// Cannot be written until implementation bodies are visible — left as a
60.     /// placeholder; the specification phase fills it in.
61.     pub closed spec fn internal_inv(self) -> bool {
62.         true
63.     }
64. }
65. ```
66. 
67. ## Well-formedness Invariant
68. 
69. ```rust
70. impl IdentityMapView {
71.     pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {
72.         &&& self.internal_inv()
73.         // Every recorded page is identified by a page-aligned base address.
74.         &&& (forall|p: usize| self.mapped.contains(p) ==> is_page_aligned(p))
75.         // Before initialization no lazy mapping has been installed; coverage
76.         // is provided entirely by the boot page tables.
77.         &&& (!self.initialized ==> self.mapped =~= Set::empty())
78.     }
79. }
80. ```
81. 
82. `is_page_aligned(p) := p % PAGE_SIZE == 0` is a free spec helper (constant
83. resolved in the spec phase). Both conjuncts are abstraction-level truths any
84. implementation maintains, not statements about a particular layout.
85. 
86. Monotonicity ("a mapped page is never unmapped or remapped") is a property of
87. *transitions*, so it lives in `ensures` (e.g. `old@.mapped.subset_of(self@.mapped)`),
88. not in `inv()`.
89. 
90. ## Spec Transition / Query Functions
91. 
92. ```rust
93. impl IdentityMapView {
94.     /// Page is reachable at its own physical address right now.
95.     /// Before init, the boot tables make every page reachable; after init,
96.     /// reachability is exactly membership in `mapped`. This is the headline
97.     /// resource callers obtain from `identity_map_page` on `Ok`.
98.     pub open spec fn accessible(self, page: usize) -> bool {
99.         !self.initialized || self.mapped.contains(page)
100.     }
101. 
102.     /// Unconditional install of one page (idempotent). Models the leaf step
103.     /// `ensure_pte` realizes: it always adds the page to the map.
104.     pub open spec fn spec_install_page(self, page: usize) -> IdentityMapView {
105.         IdentityMapView { mapped: self.mapped.insert(page), ..self }
106.     }
107. 
108.     /// Full effect of `identity_map_page`: install the page when the mapper is
109.     /// initialized, otherwise a no-op (boot tables already cover it). Either
110.     /// way the page ends up `accessible`.
111.     pub open spec fn spec_map_page(self, page: usize) -> IdentityMapView {
112.         if self.initialized {
113.             self.spec_install_page(page)
114.         } else {
115.             self
116.         }
117.     }
118. }
119. ```
120. 
121. ### How each in-scope function uses the View
122. 
123. | Function | View-level effect | Notes |
124. |----------|-------------------|-------|
125. | `identity_map_page(phys_addr)` | `self@ == old@.spec_map_page(base(phys_addr@))`; on `Ok`, `self@.accessible(base(phys_addr@))` | `base(a) := align_down(a, PAGE_SIZE)`; equals `a` for the page-aligned input. On `Err`, `self@ == old@` and the page need not be accessible. |
126. | `ensure_pte(pt, pte_idx, phys_addr)` | `self@ == old@.spec_install_page(base(phys_addr))` (idempotent) | The leaf step that realizes V==P; `identity_map_page` wraps it with the `initialized` guard. |
127. | `ensure_pt(pd, pde_idx)` | `self@.mapped == old@.mapped` (identity at the page abstraction) | Allocating/installing a page table establishes *internal structure* only — its PTEs start absent, so no page becomes mapped. Returns an opaque page-aligned `pt_paddr`. Idempotent: a present PDE leaves state unchanged. Also called by `init` to pre-allocate. |
128. 
129. The two private helpers deliberately have **no PDE/PTE-index fields in the
130. View**: the caller analysis states callers "don't care about the page-directory /
131. page-table index split." `ensure_pt` contributes nothing to `mapped`; only
132. `ensure_pte` does. Their composition inside `identity_map_page` is exactly
133. `spec_map_page`.
134. 
135. ## Design Rationale
136. 
137. **`initialized: bool`** — The contract has a genuine pre-init mode: before `init`
138. publishes the kernel PD, `identity_map_page` succeeds as a no-op and the page is
139. reachable through boot tables. This flag is the minimal abstract state needed to
140. state that conditional transition (`spec_map_page`) and to make `accessible`
141. total. *Substitution test:* any lazy-mapper implementation has a "not yet set up,
142. boot tables cover memory" phase versus an "active" phase; the flag survives a
143. rewrite. It is never a stand-in for the concrete `KERNEL_PD_PADDR == 0` check —
144. callers observe a *mode*, not an atomic.
145. 
146. **`mapped: Set<usize>`** — The core resource: which physical pages are
147. identity-mapped (present + writable + supervisor). Callers reason purely in terms
148. of set membership ("is my frame reachable?"), and idempotence/monotonicity are
149. naturally `insert` / `subset_of` on a `Set`. *Substitution test:* every possible
150. implementation — two-level x86 tables, a flat array, a different paging scheme —
151. must track *which pages are mapped*; the set is implementation-agnostic. Elements
152. are page-aligned base addresses (`usize`) because callers already hold
153. `PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>` and the skill keeps addresses as `usize`; this
154. avoids introducing division/frame-number arithmetic at the abstraction surface.
155. 
156. **Permissions encoded by membership, not a field** — These functions only ever
157. create writable, supervisor mappings, so per-page permission state would be a
158. constant. Folding "writable + supervisor" into the meaning of `mapped`
159. membership keeps the View minimal while still letting `KernelFrame::clear` /
160. `memset` rely on writability.
161. 
162. **`accessible` as a derived query** — Gives callers a single predicate for the
163. postcondition they actually want ("the frame is reachable now") that is uniform
164. across the pre-init and post-init cases, so caller proofs don't branch on
165. `initialized`.
166. 
167. **`inv()` conjuncts** — `is_page_aligned` over `mapped` is the abstraction's
168. well-formedness (a "page" is a page-aligned unit). The `!initialized ==> mapped
169. empty` conjunct is the cross-field consistency that justifies `spec_map_page`'s
170. no-op branch (nothing is silently dropped when not initialized). Both are
171. caller-visible truths and hold for any implementation.
172. 
173. **Field usage (minimality check)** — `initialized` is used in `spec_map_page`,
174. `accessible`, and `inv`; `mapped` is used in every spec function. No field is
175. dead.
176. 
177. | Criterion | Result |
178. |-----------|--------|
179. | Substitution | ✅ both fields survive a full rewrite |
180. | Caller-only | ✅ no PDE/PTE indices, flag bits, BSS-pool, or CR3 mechanics leak |
181. | Complete | ✅ accessibility, idempotence, monotonicity, pre-init no-op all expressible |
182. | Minimal | ✅ two fields, both referenced by specs |
183. | No code-as-spec | ✅ describes *which pages are mapped*, not *how* |
184. 
185. ## Rejected Alternatives
186. 
187. - **Two-level `Map<TableIndex, Map<TableIndex, usize>>` (PD → PT → frame).**
188.   Mirrors the x86 page-table structure and the `ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte` split.
189.   Rejected: the caller analysis explicitly says external callers don't care about
190.   the PD/PT index split or `Table::from_address` mechanics — this is an
191.   abstraction leak (Over-Faithful anti-pattern). The page-granular `Set` captures
192.   everything callers observe.
193. 
194. - **`mapped: Set<nat>` keyed by frame number (`addr / PAGE_SIZE`).** Equivalent
195.   power, but forces division semantics into the abstraction and diverges from the
196.   `PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>` (a `usize`) callers actually pass. Page-aligned
197.   `usize` base addresses are more directly usable in caller specs.
198. 
199. - **Per-page permission/flags field (e.g. `Map<usize, Perms>`).** All mappings
200.   are uniformly writable + supervisor, so this would store a constant. Encoded by
201.   `mapped` membership instead.
202. 
203. - **A `pt_pool_used: nat` / remaining-BSS-slots field.** Callers explicitly don't
204.   care about page-table-pool bookkeeping; `OutOfMemory` is observed only as an
205.   `Err`. Exhaustion is a failure outcome, not abstract state callers reason about.
206.   Belongs (if anywhere) inside `internal_inv()`, not the public View.
207. 
208. - **`kernel_pd_paddr: usize` / `cr3` fields.** These are concrete handles to the
209.   paging structures, not caller-observable abstract state. Callers never name the
210.   kernel PD address; replacing it (or the CR3 root) with a different mechanism
211.   must not change the spec. Leaking them fails the substitution test.
212. 
213. - **A separate per-`Table` View for `ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte`.** Tempting because
214.   they take a `Table` argument, but they are private sub-steps of a single global
215.   operation; giving them independent View types would fragment the abstraction and
216.   re-expose the index structure. They are specified as refinements of
217.   `spec_install_page` / the identity transition on the one global
218.   `IdentityMapView`.
219. 
220. - **No `initialized` flag (treat init as just another mapping).** Then
221.   `identity_map_page`'s pre-init no-op success could not be stated precisely, and
222.   `accessible` would wrongly require `mapped` membership during early boot. The
223.   flag is the minimal addition that captures the documented pre-init transparency.
224.

57. ## Caller Expectations
58. 
59. ### `identity_map_page(phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>) -> Result<(), Error>`
60. 
61. This is the only externally-visible (`pub(crate)`) in-scope function. The principal
62. external caller is `KernelFrame::new`, which must make a freshly-allocated physical
63. frame accessible through the kernel's identity map before handing out a `KernelFrame`
64. whose `Deref`/`DerefMut` dereference that physical address.
65. 
66. - **Callers assume on `Ok(())`:**
67.   - The page containing `phys_addr` is present and identity-mapped (V==P) in the kernel
68.     page directory, i.e. the page can subsequently be read/written through its physical
69.     address while the kernel address space is active. `KernelFrame::new` relies on this so
70.     that later `deref`/`deref_mut`/`clear` on the frame are sound.
71.   - The operation is **idempotent / no-op safe**: if the PTE is already present,
72.     nothing changes and `Ok(())` is still returned. Callers may map the same page
73.     repeatedly (e.g. multiple `KernelFrame`s over the same frame, or overlapping ranges
74.     in `memcpy`/`memset`).
75.   - The mapping has supervisor + read/write permissions (callers need to write frames,
76.     e.g. `KernelFrame::clear`, `memset`).
77.   - The TLB is consistent for the mapped page (a new mapping invalidates the stale TLB
78.     entry via `invlpg`), so the very next access through `phys_addr` sees the new mapping.
79.   - **Pre-init no-op:** if the lazy mapper is not yet initialized (`KERNEL_PD_PADDR == 0`,
80.     boot page tables still active), the call is a no-op returning `Ok(())`. Early-boot
81.     callers rely on this to succeed before `init` runs.
82.   - No physical frame is consumed from the frame allocator (page tables come from the BSS
83.     pool), so callers can use this from within frame-allocation paths (`KernelFrame::new`)
84.     without recursive frame allocation / deadlock.
85. 
86. - **Callers assume on `Err(e)`:**
87.   - The frame was *not* made accessible; the caller must not dereference it.
88.     `KernelFrame::new` propagates the error and does **not** construct the `KernelFrame`.
89.   - The error is a `sys::error::Error`; observed codes are `InvalidArgument` (failed PDE/PTE
90.     read), `OutOfMemory` (BSS PT pool exhausted, via `ensure_pt`), and `BadAddress`
91.     (frame number out of range). Callers branch on `Result`, not on the specific code.
92. 
93. - **Callers don't care about:**
94.   - Whether a new page table had to be allocated/installed (PDE absent) or the PDE was
95.     already present — only that the final PTE is present.
96.   - The page-directory / page-table index split (`pd_index`/`pt_index`), the BSS pool
97.     bump-allocator mechanics, or the `Table::from_address` raw-pointer construction.
98.   - The concrete PTE/PDE flag bit layout, beyond "present, writable, supervisor".
99.   - The internal split between `ensure_pt` and `ensure_pte`.
100. 
101. ### `ensure_pt(pd: Table<PageDirectoryEntry>, pde_idx: TableIndex) -> Result<usize, Error>`
102. 
103. Private; callers are `init` and `identity_map_page` only.
104. 
105. - **Callers assume on `Ok(pt_paddr)`:**
106.   - The PDE at `pde_idx` in `pd` is present after the call, and `pt_paddr` is the
107.     physical address of the page table it points to (page-aligned, BSS-backed, all PTEs
108.     initially absent if freshly allocated).
109.   - Idempotent: if the PDE was already present, the *existing* PT's frame address is
110.     returned and the PDE is left unchanged. `init` relies on this to be safe to call once
111.     per PDE; `identity_map_page` relies on it so repeated maps reuse the same PT.
112.   - `pt_paddr` is immediately usable as `Table::from_address(pt_paddr)` for a follow-up
113.     `ensure_pte` (i.e. it is identity-mapped / directly addressable).
114. - **Callers assume on `Err`:** the PDE may be unchanged and no usable PT address is
115.   produced; the caller (`identity_map_page`, `init`) propagates the error with `?`.
116.   `OutOfMemory` specifically signals BSS PT-pool exhaustion.
117. - **Callers don't care about:** the allocator slot bookkeeping, the exact flag set written
118.   into the new PDE, or whether allocation happened.
119. 
120. ### `ensure_pte(pt: Table<PageTableEntry>, pte_idx: TableIndex, phys_addr: usize) -> Result<(), Error>`
121. 
122. Private; sole caller is `identity_map_page`.
123. 
124. - **Callers assume on `Ok(())`:**
125.   - The PTE at `pte_idx` in `pt` is present and maps to the frame containing `phys_addr`
126.     (identity mapping, writable, supervisor). This is the step that actually realizes the
127.     V==P guarantee `identity_map_page` promises its callers.
128.   - Idempotent: if the PTE was already present it is left unchanged (no re-write, no extra
129.     `invlpg`) and `Ok(())` is returned.
130.   - On a freshly-installed mapping the corresponding TLB entry for `phys_addr` was
131.     invalidated, so the mapping is immediately effective.
132. - **Callers assume on `Err`:** the PTE was not installed; `identity_map_page` propagates
133.   the error. `BadAddress` means `phys_addr` produced an out-of-range frame number.
134. - **Callers don't care about:** the precise flag encoding or the TLB-invalidation
135.   mechanism, only that the entry is present and effective.

137. ## Abstract Resource
138. 
139. This module manages the **kernel's identity map**: a single global mapping from physical
140. addresses to equal-valued virtual addresses (V == P) for the kernel address space, backed
141. by the kernel page directory plus BSS-pooled page tables. The in-scope functions answer one
142. question for callers — *"is this physical page reachable at its own address in the kernel
143. address space?"* — and, if not, make it so without consuming frame-allocator memory.
144. 
145. Key operations (in scope): map one page (`identity_map_page`), ensure the covering page
146. table exists (`ensure_pt`), ensure the leaf entry exists (`ensure_pte`).
147. 
148. ## Key Invariants (caller perspective)
149. 
150. - **Idempotence / monotonicity:** mapping is never removed or remapped by these functions;
151.   a present PDE/PTE is left untouched. Repeated calls on the same page are safe no-ops.
152.   Once a page is identity-mapped, it stays mapped.
153. - **Post-success accessibility:** after `Ok` from `identity_map_page`, the page is present,
154.   writable, supervisor-only, and TLB-consistent in the kernel address space.
155. - **Page-table source is the BSS pool, not the frame allocator:** these functions never
156.   recurse into physical frame allocation, so they are safe to call from within frame
157.   allocation (`KernelFrame::new`).
158. - **Pre-init transparency:** before `init` publishes `KERNEL_PD_PADDR`, `identity_map_page`
159.   is a successful no-op (boot page tables already cover the relevant memory).
160. - **Failure leaves callers safe:** on `Err`, the target page must be treated as not
161.   accessible; callers do not proceed to dereference it.
162. - **Single-pass within a call:** `identity_map_page` touches exactly one PDE then one PTE
163.   (`ensure_pt` then `ensure_pte`) for the page; `pt_paddr` returned by `ensure_pt` is the
164.   table consumed by the subsequent `ensure_pte`.

174.   it simply `?`-propagates the `Result`. So there is no upstream bias to inherit — the View
175.   for this module can be designed cleanly from the expectations above.

180. `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`, so they must not be marked `external_body`. Their

183. abstract `ensures`; the raw `Table::read`/`write` and `paging::invlpg` operations are the

   - The internal split between `ensure_pt` and `ensure_pte`.
 
 ### `ensure_pt(pd: Table<PageDirectoryEntry>, pde_idx: TableIndex) -> Result<usize, Error>`
 
 Private; callers are `init` and `identity_map_page` only.
 
 - **Callers assume on `Ok(pt_paddr)`:**
   - The PDE at `pde_idx` in `pd` is present after the call, and `pt_paddr` is the
     physical address of the page table it points to (page-aligned, BSS-backed, all PTEs
     initially absent if freshly allocated).

     returned and the PDE is left unchanged. `init` relies on this to be safe to call once
     per PDE; `identity_map_page` relies on it so repeated maps reuse the same PT.
   - `pt_paddr` is immediately usable as `Table::from_address(pt_paddr)` for a follow-up
     `ensure_pte` (i.e. it is identity-mapped / directly addressable).

   produced; the caller (`identity_map_page`, `init`) propagates the error with `?`.

   into the new PDE, or whether allocation happened.
 
 ### `ensure_pte(pt: Table<PageTableEntry>, pte_idx: TableIndex, phys_addr: usize) -> Result<(), Error>`
 
 Private; sole caller is `identity_map_page`.

   - The PTE at `pte_idx` in `pt` is present and maps to the frame containing `phys_addr`
     (identity mapping, writable, supervisor). This is the step that actually realizes the
     V==P guarantee `identity_map_page` promises its callers.
   - Idempotent: if the PTE was already present it is left unchanged (no re-write, no extra
     `invlpg`) and `Ok(())` is returned.

     invalidated, so the mapping is immediately effective.

   the error. `BadAddress` means `phys_addr` produced an out-of-range frame number.

   mechanism, only that the entry is present and effective.

 This module manages the **kernel's identity map**: a single global mapping from physical
 addresses to equal-valued virtual addresses (V == P) for the kernel address space, backed
 by the kernel page directory plus BSS-pooled page tables. The in-scope functions answer one
 question for callers — *"is this physical page reachable at its own address in the kernel
 address space?"* — and, if not, make it so without consuming frame-allocator memory.

 table exists (`ensure_pt`), ensure the leaf entry exists (`ensure_pte`).

 - **Idempotence / monotonicity:** mapping is never removed or remapped by these functions;

   Once a page is identity-mapped, it stays mapped.

   writable, supervisor-only, and TLB-consistent in the kernel address space.

   recurse into physical frame allocation, so they are safe to call from within frame
   allocation (`KernelFrame::new`).
 - **Pre-init transparency:** before `init` publishes `KERNEL_PD_PADDR`, `identity_map_page`
   is a successful no-op (boot page tables already cover the relevant memory).
 - **Failure leaves callers safe:** on `Err`, the target page must be treated as not
   accessible; callers do not proceed to dereference it.
 - **Single-pass within a call:** `identity_map_page` touches exactly one PDE then one PTE
   (`ensure_pt` then `ensure_pte`) for the page; `pt_paddr` returned by `ensure_pt` is the
   table consumed by the subsequent `ensure_pte`.

   marked `#[verus_verify(external_body)]` with its own `requires/ensures` (over the frame
   abstraction `kf@ == base@`). It does **not** impose any spec onto `identity_map_page`;
   it simply `?`-propagates the `Result`. So there is no upstream bias to inherit — the View
   for this module can be designed cleanly from the expectations above.

 `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`, so they must not be marked `external_body`. Their

 abstract `ensures`; the raw `Table::read`/`write` and `paging::invlpg` operations are the
 trusted HAL boundary these functions build on.

 - `src/kernel/src/hal/mem/types/address/frame.rs::FrameAddress::into_raw_value` — the raw value is
   the abstract frame address (`ensures result as int == self@`). Verified when the address layer is.
 
 ## `external_body` introduced while speccing `mm::virt::identity_map`
 
 These three exec functions realize the V==P identity mapping through the page-table hardware
 trust boundary. Each carries its **full** `#[verus_spec]` contract unchanged (no spec weakening);
 the `external_body` only trusts the *body* until the `mm::virt` page-table permission ghost token
 is realized. This is the same deferred-ghost-token class as `table::write`
 (no contents `ensures`) and `kframe::new` (the caller already TCB-listed *because* it calls
 `identity_map_page`). All three were verified-by-`admit()` in the spec phase; the `admit()` is now
 replaced by the codebase-sanctioned `external_body` + this listing.
 
 - `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs::ensure_pt` — body calls
   `PAGE_TABLE_ALLOCATOR.alloc_as::<[PteWord; PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH]>()`, whose contract carries
   `requires bump_view(self).inv()` (`src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs:350`). `bump_view` is a
   parameter-free `uninterp spec fn` with **no** establishing lemma and **no** `type_invariant`
   anywhere in `src/libs/bump_allocator/` (verified: `grep -rn "bump_view" src` filtered to
   `ensures|broadcast|axiom|proof fn|type_invariant` returns nothing). That `inv()` is the bump
   allocator's own deferred ghost token — it is **not** derivable from `ensure_pt`'s sole
   precondition `identity_map_view().inv()`, so the alloc-path obligation cannot be discharged
   in-body. Same cross-module deferral class as `kframe::new`. Contract preserved verbatim:
   `Ok(pt_paddr) => identity_map_view().inv() && spec_is_page_aligned(pt_paddr)`,
   `Err(_) => identity_map_view().inv()`.
 - `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs::ensure_pte` — installs the leaf PTE via
   `Table::<PageTableEntry>::write`, which is deliberately **contents-free**
   (`external_body`, only `requires index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`, no contents `ensures`; a contents
   postcondition is documented-unsound — see the `table::write` entry above). There is therefore no
   spec link from a concrete PTE write to the parameter-free `identity_map_view().mapped`, so the
   `mapped.contains(spec_page_base(phys_addr))` postcondition is the deferred page-table permission
   token (the `identity_map_view()` `v -> v'` transition). Contract preserved verbatim:
   `Ok(_) => identity_map_view().inv() && identity_map_view().mapped.contains(spec_page_base(phys_addr))`,
   `Err(_) => identity_map_view().inv() && !...contains(...)`.
 - `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs::identity_map_page` — composes a `KERNEL_PD_PADDR`
   atomic load with `ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte`. No spec links the atomic load + sub-call composition
   to the parameter-free `identity_map_view()`, so the `accessible(phys_addr)` postcondition rests
   on the same `mm::virt` token. Note `kframe::new` is **already** TCB-listed precisely *because it
   calls this function* needing the unrealized token. Contract preserved verbatim:
   `Ok(_) => identity_map_view().inv() && identity_map_view().accessible(phys_addr@)`,
   `Err(_) => identity_map_view().inv() && !...accessible(...)`.
 
 - `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.spec.rs::ExPageTableBss` —
   `#[verifier::external_type_specification]` + `#[verifier::external_body]` registration of the
   external `super::page_table_allocator::PageTableBss` BSS-pool type (the backing store for
   `PAGE_TABLE_ALLOCATOR`). Opaque external type, no fields modeled; listed for completeness so
   every in-scope `external_*` is accounted for.
 
 ## External-bottom: build-time constant accessor
 
 - `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::kernel_watermark` — `external_body` accessor that returns
   the build-time constant `config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK`. This constant is generated by the
   `config` crate's `build.rs` (from `kernel_config.toml`) and lives in a non-Verus dependency
   crate, so Verus cannot resolve its value. The accessor's `ensures ret as nat ==
   spec_kernel_watermark()` ties the runtime value to the abstract spec value. The companion spec
   function `spec_kernel_watermark()` (in `manager.spec.rs`) is therefore `uninterp` — a mechanical
   consequence of this external-bottom boundary, not a verification escape: the watermark threshold
   is genuinely outside Verus's view and callers do not depend on its concrete value (only on the
   fact that user allocations are gated by it; see `caller_analysis.md` line 121).
 
 ## `assume_specification` for not-yet-verified callees (eliminated when their module is verified)
 
 Most of these `assume_specification` (and one `external_type_specification`) declarations live
 in `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.spec.rs`; a few co-locate with the type they describe (the
 `PageAligned` ones now live in `src/kernel/src/hal/mem/types/address/aligned/page.spec.rs`,

 verified-in-body) `Inner` frame-allocator methods so those bodies translate. Each is superseded
 by the real specification when its module is verified — the same "superseded when the address
 layer is verified" rationale already used for `FrameAddress::from_raw_value`/`into_raw_value`.
 
 - **External crate (`arch`) — genuinely outside the kernel crate, temporary placeholder:**
   - `::arch::mem::paging::FrameNumber` — `external_type_specification` (`ExFrameNumber`).
   - `::arch::mem::FRAME_SIZE` — `ensures result == spec_page_size()`.
   - `::arch::mem::paging::FrameNumber::from_raw_value` / `into_raw_value`.
   - `::arch::mem::PAGE_ALIGNMENT` — declared at
     `src/kernel/src/hal/mem/types/address/aligned/page.spec.rs:7`. `PAGE_ALIGNMENT` is a
     `pub const Alignment` in the external `arch` crate (`Alignment::Align4096`), declared
     outside any `verus!` block, so Verus cannot resolve its value and exec code referencing

     above; superseded once `arch` carries a real verified spec for `PAGE_ALIGNMENT`.

112. /// uninitialized (atomics are not published).

119. /// `[0, MEMORY_SIZE)` that does not already have one. This covers all physical memory, so no
120. /// new PDEs are created at runtime. The kernel PD and CR3 atomics are published only after
121. /// pre-allocation succeeds, so other code never observes a partially-initialized identity map.

123.     kernel_pd_paddr: PageDirectoryAddress,
124.     kernel_cr3: Cr3Register,
125. ) -> Result<(), Error> {
126.     // Pre-allocate page tables for all PDE indices in [0, MEMORY_SIZE).
127.     // This covers all physical memory, so no new PDEs are created at runtime.
128.     let pd_paddr: usize = kernel_pd_paddr.into_raw_value();
129.     let pde_count: usize = MEMORY_SIZE / mem::PGTAB_SIZE;
130.     for i in 0..pde_count {
131.         let pde_idx: TableIndex = paging::pd_index(i * mem::PGTAB_SIZE);
132.         // SAFETY: the PD is identity-mapped.
133.         let pd: Table<PageDirectoryEntry> = unsafe { Table::from_address(pd_paddr) };
134.         ensure_pt(pd, pde_idx)?;
135.     }
136. 
137.     // Publish the kernel PD and CR3 only after pre-allocation succeeds, so that other code
138.     // (e.g. `sync_kernel_pdes`, `with_kernel_address_space`) never observes a partially-
139.     // initialized identity map.
140.     KERNEL_PD_PADDR.store(kernel_pd_paddr.into_raw_value(), Ordering::Release);
141.     KERNEL_CR3.store(kernel_cr3.into_u32(), Ordering::Release);
142. 
143.     Ok(())

196.             "memcpy(): source and destination ranges overlap",

200.     with_kernel_address_space(|| {

206.         ensure_identity_mapped_range(dst_start, dst_size)?;
